findings.summary: DenStream establishes decay/pruning of streaming micro-clusters under limited memory, and Dynamic Cluster Memory (CVPR 2024) expands memory on novelty while pruning overlapping clusters to maintain fixed capacity. Mature-candidate turnover would therefore be ordinary lifecycle/resource management rather than a novel computational principle.

Adaptive Resonance Theory and related recurrent category-learning models explicitly preserve learned categories while mismatch can reset/search and recruit new representational resources. Future Assembly continual-acquisition claims therefore require matched resource and retention/adaptation comparisons rather than category persistence alone.
sources: Layher et al., Frontiers in Psychology 2014, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2014.01287
Grossberg ART literature on mismatch-triggered reset/search/category recruitment

findings.summary: Associative pattern completion in CA3 and recurrent category-learning models depends on recurrent/top-down causal interactions. A post-field Assembly recognizer that changes readout without changing lower field dynamics is not itself a completion/regeneration mechanism.
sources: Le Duigou et al., Frontiers in Cellular Neuroscience 2014, DOI 10.3389/fncel.2013.00262
Layher et al., Frontiers in Psychology 2014, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2014.01287

findings.summary: Natural forgetting literature frames engram accessibility as dynamically remodeled and environmentally sensitive. Biological assembly/en​gram analogy therefore cannot justify permanent mature entries; persistence versus decay/remodeling must be an explicit computational lifecycle contract.
sources: Ryan & Frankland, Nature Reviews Neuroscience 2022, DOI 10.1038/s41583-021-00548-3
